problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: Minimize the convex robust objective F(x)=sup_w E[w(ξ)loss(x,ξ)] over a closed convex domain. Feasible densities satisfy w≥0, E[w]=1, w∈L², and E[(w−1)²]/2≤ρ.
problem_class.evidence: LongTails/Setups/ChiSquareConstrainedDro.lean: IsFeasibleDensity, objective, spec.admissible convex-domain and sample-subgradient inequalities.

problem_class.label: other
problem_class.details: Population distributionally robust optimization with a χ²-divergence constraint of public radius ρ>0.

oracle.label: stochastic_gradient
oracle.details: Each call uses a fresh IID sample ξ and returns a sample-loss subgradient at the projected query. It is not stipulated to be an unbiased subgradient of the robust objective.

oracle.label: function_value
oracle.details: The same call returns loss(projection(y),ξ), jointly with its sample subgradient.

oracle.label: other
oracle.details: Each oracle reply also returns the exact metric projection of the query onto the hidden domain. Projection is bundled into the counted oracle call.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/ChiSquareConstrainedDro.lean: sampleOracle.answer and spec.admissible projection variational inequality; LongTails/Template.lean: executeWithTrace.

distinctive_assumptions.label: bounded_variance
distinctive_assumptions.details: Sample subgradients satisfy ‖sub(x,ξ)‖≤G pointwise, hence have second moment at most G². Losses satisfy 0≤loss(x,ξ)≤B pointwise.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: The ambient space is a complete real Hilbert space with second-countable Borel topology. A robust minimizer x* exists with ‖x0−x*‖≤R; the domain need not be bounded. Public information comprises the spaces, ρ,G,B,R,ε,x0, with ρ,G,B,ε>0 and R≥0. The loss, subgradient map, sampling law, and domain are hidden instance data.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/ChiSquareConstrainedDro.lean: Params, Instance, spec.Public, spec.publicInput, spec.valid, and spec.admissible minimizer condition.

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: Return a measurable output lying in the domain for every outcome, with integrable robust objective gap F(output)−F(x*) and expectation at most ε.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: The objective-gap guarantee is in expectation over algorithm randomness and the IID oracle stream, under a fixed oracle-call budget.
accuracy.evidence: LongTails/Setups/ChiSquareConstrainedDro.lean: spec.successful; LongTails/Template.lean: Convergence and executeWithTrace; supplied extracted result budget.

setup_category.reason: χ²-constrained population DRO with bounded convex sample losses, IID sampling, and expected objective-gap accuracy is an established optimization formulation.

descriptionHtml:
Chi-Square Constrained Robust Optimization

We minimize a robust objective F over a closed convex set C in a separable real Hilbert space E. Here F(x) is the worst expected sample loss under nonnegative densities relative to a probability law ν, with mean one and chi-square divergence at most ρ>0. Sample losses are jointly measurable, convex and bounded on C, with jointly measurable bounded subgradients. Each oracle call returns the projection of the query onto C, together with its loss and subgradient evaluated using one fresh independent sample from ν. Given ε>0, the goal is a measurable feasible output x¯ with E[F(x¯)−F(x⋆)]≤ε, where x⋆ minimizes F on C and expectation includes sampling and algorithm randomness.

Let Ξ be a measurable sample space carrying the probability measure ν. Write ℓ:E×Ξ→R for the sample loss and g:E×Ξ→E for its supplied subgradient. Define the density class Wρ={w:Ξ→R measurable:w(ξ)≥0 for every ξ,w∈L2(ν),Eξ∼ν[w(ξ)]=1,12Eξ∼ν[(w(ξ)−1)2]≤ρ}. The objective and optimization problem are F(x)=supw∈WρEξ∼ν[w(ξ)ℓ(x,ξ)],minx∈CF(x). The norm ∥⋅∥ is induced by the inner product on E. The algorithm receives E, Ξ, ρ>0, G>0, B>0, R≥0, ε>0, and a given point x0∈E; the instance consists of C, ν, ℓ, and g, accessed through the oracle described below.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Feasible set and projection). The set C⊆E is closed and convex, and x0∈C. There is a measurable map ΠC:E→C satisfying ⟨y−ΠC(y),u−ΠC(y)⟩≤0,y∈E,u∈C.

Assumption 2 (Sample losses and subgradients). The maps ℓ and g are jointly measurable. For every ξ∈Ξ and x,y∈C, ℓ(x,ξ)+⟨g(x,ξ),y−x⟩≤ℓ(y,ξ),0≤ℓ(x,ξ)≤B,∥g(x,ξ)∥≤G.

Assumption 3 (Initial distance). There exists x⋆∈C such that F(x⋆)≤F(x)for every x∈C,∥x0−x⋆∥≤R.

Queries may be made at any y∈E. At call k≥0, the oracle returns (ΠC(y), ℓ(ΠC(y),ξk), g(ΠC(y),ξk)). The sample variables (ξk)k≥0 are measurable, mutually independent, and each has law ν. The loss and subgradient in a reply use the same sample. Any algorithm randomness is independent of the entire sample sequence.

After the allotted calls, the output x¯ must be measurable and belong to C for every realization. Its objective gap must be integrable and satisfy EP[F(x¯)−F(x⋆)]≤ε, where P is the joint law of the samples and the algorithm’s randomness.

comparisonHtml:
Let X be a nonempty closed convex subset of a complete, second-countable real inner-product space with its Borel measurable structure. The population law P0 is arbitrary. Jointly measurable losses and subgradients satisfy 0≤ℓ(x;ξ)≤B, convex subgradient inequalities on X, and ∥g(x;ξ)∥≤G. A minimizer x⋆∈X satisfies ∥x0−x⋆∥≤R, with x0∈X, ρ,G,B,ε>0 and R≥0. Each IID oracle call returns projection onto X, loss, and subgradient. Define L(x)=sup{∫wℓ(x;ξ)dP0:w≥0, w∈L2(P0), ∫wdP0=1, 12∫(w−1)2dP0≤ρ}. The target is a measurable feasible output x^ with ∫[L(x^(ω))−L(x⋆)]dP(ω)≤ε under the IID sampling law P.

(1): at ρ≥1, GR=B, costs O(ρB2ε−2Λ2) versus O(ρB3ε−3Γ2) for ε≪B. Scope: initial-distance bound replaces diameter bound. Deterministic budget includes selection. (1) loses for ρ≪min{B2/(G2R2),εB/(GR)} through B2/(ρε2). For ρ≥1, gain requires ε≲G2R2B/(G2R2+B2), up to logarithms.

Abbr: Λ=log(2+(1+ρ)Bρε); Γ=1+log⁡(1+ρB/ε2); ρ is the χ2 radius; G bounds subgradient norms; B bounds losses; R bounds initial distance (diameter for (2)). ≲ and ≪ describe comparison regimes; rate gains are up to logarithmic factors.

import LongTails.Setups.StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Function.L2Space

open MeasureTheory
open scoped RealInnerProductSpace

namespace LongTails.Setups.ChiSquareConstrainedDro

open OracleTemplate

structure Params where
  E : Type u
  [normedE : NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [linearE : InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  [completeE : CompleteSpace E]
  [measurableE : MeasurableSpace E]
  [borelE : BorelSpace E]
  [countableE : SecondCountableTopology E]
  Ξ : Type
  [measurableΞ : MeasurableSpace Ξ]
  ρ : ℝ
  G : ℝ
  B : ℝ
  R : ℝ
  ε : ℝ
  x0 : E

attribute [instance] Params.normedE Params.linearE Params.completeE Params.measurableE
  Params.borelE Params.countableE Params.measurableΞ

structure Instance (q : Params) where
  loss : q.E → q.Ξ → ℝ
  sub : q.E → q.Ξ → q.E
  law : ProbabilityMeasure q.Ξ
  domain : Set q.E

def IsFeasibleDensity {q : Params} (I : Instance q) (w : q.Ξ → ℝ) : Prop :=
  Measurable w ∧ (∀ ξ, 0 ≤ w ξ) ∧ MemLp w 2 (I.law : Measure q.Ξ) ∧
    (∫ ξ, w ξ ∂(I.law : Measure q.Ξ)) = 1 ∧
    (∫ ξ, (w ξ - 1) ^ 2 ∂(I.law : Measure q.Ξ)) / 2 ≤ q.ρ

noncomputable def objective {q : Params} (I : Instance q) (x : q.E) : ℝ :=
  sSup {v | ∃ w, IsFeasibleDensity I w ∧ v = ∫ ξ, w ξ * I.loss x ξ ∂(I.law : Measure q.Ξ)}

noncomputable def sampleOracle {q : Params} (I : Instance q) (projection : q.E → q.E)
    (P : ProbabilityMeasure (ℕ → q.Ξ)) : Oracle q.E (q.E × ℝ × q.E) where
  Seed := fun _ => q.Ξ
  law := P
  answer := fun _ (_, y) seed =>
    (projection y, I.loss (projection y) seed, I.sub (projection y) seed)

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  Instance := Instance
  Query q := q.E
  Reply q := q.E × ℝ × q.E
  Output q := q.E
  publicInput q := q
  valid q := 0 < q.ρ ∧ 0 < q.G ∧ 0 < q.B ∧ 0 ≤ q.R ∧ 0 < q.ε
  admissible q I O :=
    ∃ (projection : q.E → q.E) (P : ProbabilityMeasure (ℕ → q.Ξ)),
    LongTails.Setups.StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.IID (fun k (ξ : ℕ → q.Ξ) => ξ k)
      (I.law : Measure q.Ξ) (P : Measure _) ∧
    O = sampleOracle I projection P ∧
    Convex ℝ I.domain ∧ IsClosed I.domain ∧ q.x0 ∈ I.domain ∧
    Measurable projection ∧
    (∀ x, projection x ∈ I.domain) ∧
    (∀ x, ∀ u ∈ I.domain, ⟪x - projection x, u - projection x⟫ ≤ 0) ∧
    Measurable (Function.uncurry I.loss) ∧
    Measurable (Function.uncurry I.sub) ∧
    (∀ ξ, ∀ x ∈ I.domain, ∀ y ∈ I.domain, I.loss x ξ + ⟪I.sub x ξ, y - x⟫ ≤ I.loss y ξ) ∧
    (∀ ξ, ∀ x ∈ I.domain, 0 ≤ I.loss x ξ ∧ I.loss x ξ ≤ q.B) ∧
    (∀ ξ, ∀ x ∈ I.domain, ‖I.sub x ξ‖ ≤ q.G) ∧
    (∃ xstar ∈ I.domain, IsMinOn (objective I) I.domain xstar ∧ ‖q.x0 - xstar‖ ≤ q.R)
  successful q I output P :=
    Measurable output ∧ (∀ ω, output ω ∈ I.domain) ∧
    ∃ xstar ∈ I.domain, IsMinOn (objective I) I.domain xstar ∧
      Integrable (fun ω => objective I (output ω) - objective I xstar) (P : Measure _) ∧
      (∫ ω, objective I (output ω) - objective I xstar ∂(P : Measure _)) ≤ q.ε

end LongTails.Setups.ChiSquareConstrainedDro
